lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: How's your dissertation going?
lines.translation: 你的毕业论文进展得怎么样了？

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I'm proofreading my first draft and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.
lines.translation: 我正在校对初稿，明天就会提交给我的教授。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Oh, I haven't even started writing mine yet, so I'm really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.
lines.translation: 哦，我的论文甚至连写都还没开始呢，所以我非常担心下学期末能不能写完。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: You mean you haven't even begun yours yet?
lines.translation: 你是说你连开篇都还没动吗？

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: The final draft is due in five months.
lines.translation: 最终稿五个月后就要交了。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Of course I've started it, but I can't get to the writing yet as I haven't found enough resources to use, so I'm still researching the topic.
lines.translation: 我当然已经开始了，但因为还没找到足够的参考资料，所以还无法动笔，现在仍在调研这个课题。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Maybe the problem is the way you're doing your research.
lines.translation: 也许问题出在你的研究方法上。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information.
lines.translation: 我一开始是先和教授聊了聊应该去哪里找资料。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: And based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the Internet.
lines.translation: 在此基础上，我在图书馆找到了相关书籍，并在网上查到了许多权威的期刊论文。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I've tried all that, but don't have enough to write the dissertation as my department's minimum length is 70 pages.
lines.translation: 这些我都试过了，但我们系的论文篇幅最少要70页，我现有的资料还是不够写毕业论文。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I think the problem is that my topic isn't viable.
lines.translation: 我觉得问题在于我的选题不太可行。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: And honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material.
lines.translation: 而且说实话，我的教授一刚开始确实警告过我，可能找不到足够的资料。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: But I was so interested in the topic that I didn't let his advice deter me.
lines.translation: 但我当时对这个课题太感兴趣了，所以没有被他的建议劝退。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Well, I suggest you find a new topic.
lines.translation: 好吧，那我建议你换个新选题。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: After all, our professors are here to guide us, so it's best to listen to them.
lines.translation: 毕竟教授是来指导我们的，所以最好还是听他们的听劝。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: In retrospect, I wish I had listened to him, but I didn't.
lines.translation: 现在回想起来，我真希望当时听了他的话，可惜我没听。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: And now I don't want to give up my topic as I've already invested so much time and energy.
lines.translation: 而现在我又不想放弃这个课题，因为我已经投入了这么多时间和精力。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: If you're committed to your current topic, maybe you could make some adjustments rather than abandon it completely.
lines.translation: 如果你决定坚持用现在的课题，也许可以做一些调整，而不是彻底放弃它。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: What is your topic?
lines.translation: 你的选题是什么？

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: It's "Depictions of Femininity and Folklore from the South of the Country".
lines.translation: 是《该国南部民间传说中的女性特质刻画》。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: That's pretty narrow.
lines.translation: 那确实挺窄的。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: You could find more material if you made the topic broader, maybe by including other kinds of depictions.
lines.translation: 如果你把选题放大一点，比如把其他类型的刻画也纳入进来，可能会找到更多资料。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Broadening the topic is a great idea.
lines.translation: 扩大选题是个绝妙的主意。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I'll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.
lines.translation: 我打算先从把该国其他地区的民间传说纳入进来开始。

lines.speaker: Q1.
lines.text: What does the woman say about her dissertation?
lines.translation: 关于这位女士的毕业论文，她说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q2.
lines.text: What does the man say about his professor?
lines.translation: 关于这位男士的教授，他说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q3.
lines.text: What does the woman say about her professor?
lines.translation: 关于这位女士的教授，她说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q4.
lines.text: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?
lines.translation: 我们得知这位女士为了完成毕业论文将会怎么做？

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Today, on Book Talk, we are lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight.
lines.translation: 欢迎收看今天的《读书访谈》，我们有幸邀请到了约翰·罗宾斯，一起来聊聊他的新书——《为什么美国人这么胖以及我们该如何减肥》。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: John isn't just a respected writer; he's also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today.
lines.translation: 约翰不仅是一位受人尊敬的作家，他也是当今少有的撰写科学类著作的名人作家。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Thanks for having me, Rebecca, but I'm hardly a celebrity.
lines.translation: 谢谢你的邀请，丽贝卡，但我算不上什么名人。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: That's very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of seven million copies worldwide, and they've been translated into 12 different languages.
lines.translation: 你太谦虚了，要知道你的四本书在全球总共卖出了700万册，并且被翻译成了12种不同的语言。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: What makes people so fascinated with your work?
lines.translation: 是什么让人们对你的作品如此着迷呢？

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight or obese.
lines.translation: 这个嘛，人们之所以读我的书，是因为超过60%的美国人都超重或肥胖。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: And other countries are facing similar problems.
lines.translation: 而其他国家也面临着类似的问题。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.
lines.translation: 基本上，大家都想知道该如何解决这个问题。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: We certainly do.
lines.translation: 我们确实都很想知道。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: I've read your new book and it's fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand.
lines.translation: 我读了你的新书，写得太棒了，特别是你把深奥的科学转化为外行也能轻松理解的语言的方式。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: That's no small achievement.
lines.translation: 这可是一个不小的成就。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I'm glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried when I wrote it that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience.
lines.translation: 很高兴听到你觉得这本书通俗易懂。因为在写作时，我还担心讨论这些科学知识会让它变得更适合专业读者。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: My last book was written primarily for the medical community.
lines.translation: 我的上一本书主要是为医学界写的。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: But this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.
lines.translation: 但这一次，我想帮助普通人掌控自己的体重。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: And how do you suggest they do that?
lines.translation: 那你建议他们怎么做呢？

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight?
lines.translation: 对于想要减肥的人，你能给我们讲讲核心建议吗？

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body's needs.
lines.translation: 简而言之，我的观点是每个人都需要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃符合自己身体需求的食物。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: I don't advocate one single diet.
lines.translation: 我不提倡单一的饮食法。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others.
lines.translation: 有的人应该比别人摄入更多的碳水化合物。

lines.speaker: M:
lines.text: And different people need different amounts of protein and fat.
lines.translation: 不同的人对蛋白质和脂肪的需求量也不同。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating ten servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day.
lines.translation: 不过你确实有一些适合所有人的建议，比如每天吃10份蔬菜和3份水果。

lines.speaker: W:
lines.text: We'll talk about those recommendations next, but now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.
lines.translation: 接下来我们就会聊聊这些建议，但现在我们需要稍作休息，进一段赞助商广告。

lines.speaker: Q5.
lines.text: What does the woman say about the man in her introduction?
lines.translation: 这位女士在介绍中关于这位男士说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q6.
lines.text: What has motivated the man to write his books?
lines.translation: 是什么促使这位男士撰写他的这些书？

lines.speaker: Q7.
lines.text: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?
lines.translation: 这位男士说他的上一本书主要是写给谁的？

lines.speaker: Q8.
lines.text: What does the man recommend people do?
lines.translation: 这位男士建议人们怎么做？

lines.text: Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body.
lines.translation: 压力常常被描绘成负面的，但研究表明，适度的压力对你的大脑和身体都有好处。

lines.text: First, the benefits for the brain.
lines.translation: 首先是它对大脑的益处。

lines.text: Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning.
lines.translation: 研究表明，短时间的压力实际上可以增强认知功能。

lines.text: Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new ) brain cells.
lines.translation: 研究人员发现，将大鼠置于压力环境中仅仅几个小时，其新生大脑细胞的增长就会翻倍。

lines.text: The rats also did better on a memory test later on.
lines.translation: 随后，这些大鼠在记忆测试中的表现也更好。

lines.text: Scientists think the same thing happens in humans.
lines.translation: 科学家认为同样的情况也会发生在人类身上。

lines.text: But how does stress improve memory?
lines.translation: 但压力是如何提高记忆力的呢？

lines.text: It's simple.
lines.translation: 这很简单。

lines.text: When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve.
lines.translation: 当你的大脑细胞增殖时，你的记忆力就会得到提升。

lines.text: Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense, ( because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future.
lines.translation: 从生物学的角度来看，这是说得通的，因为那些能更好地记住危险处境的动物，未来就能更好地规避危险。

lines.text: If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it's important to remember where and when that encounter happened.
lines.translation: 例如，如果一只动物遇到了捕食者并成功逃脱，那么记住这次遭遇发生的地点和时间就至关重要。

lines.text: Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans.
lines.translation: 专家断言，同样的原则也适用于人类。

lines.text: Now, let's turn to how stress benefits the body.
lines.translation: 现在，让我们来看看压力是如何有益于身体的。

lines.text: This may come as a surprise to laymen.
lines.translation: 对于外行来说，这可能会让人感到意外。

lines.text: But experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick.
lines.translation: 但专家表示，压力可以让你免于生病。

lines.text: Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness.
lines.translation: 科学家承认，长期慢性压力会让你更容易生病。

lines.text: But research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning.
lines.translation: 但研究表明，短时期的压力实际上能提供某些防病保护，因为它增强了你的免疫功能。

lines.text: One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness.
lines.translation: 一项研究显示，经历短暂压力的大鼠，其免疫细胞反应会激增，从而使免疫系统能更好地准备对抗疾病。

lines.text: For humans, there's even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.
lines.translation: 对人类而言，甚至有证据表明，在接种疫苗前承受一定压力有助于提高疫苗的效果。

lines.speaker: Q9.
lines.text: What did researchers discover about rats placed briefly in a stressful situation?
lines.translation: 研究人员发现被短暂置于压力环境下的大鼠有什么变化？

lines.speaker: Q10.
lines.text: Why do people tend to have clear memories of dangerous situations they have encountered?
lines.translation: 为什么人们往往对自己遭遇过的危险境况有清晰的记忆？

lines.speaker: Q11.
lines.text: What do scientists believe chronic stress can do?
lines.translation: 科学家认为慢性长期压力会导致什么？

lines.text: For many managers and people who work in leadership positions, dealing with emails is a dilemma.
lines.translation: 对于许多管理者和处于领导岗位的人来说，处理电子邮件是一个让人进退两难的困境。

lines.text: It's likely the unpredictable, uncontrollable and ongoing nature of day-to-day email in terms of volume, importance and urgency contributes to their levels of anxiety and to diminished leadership skills.
lines.translation: 日常邮件在数量、重要性和紧急程度上面临着不可预测、不可控制且源源不断的特性，这很可能加剧了他们的焦虑感，并削弱了其领导能力。

lines.text: That's because it's not unusual for many leaders to prioritize email management over people management.
lines.translation: 这是因为许多领导者将邮件管理置于人员管理之上，这并不少见。

lines.text: An obsession with managing their inbox prevents them from dealing with their employees.
lines.translation: 对打理收件箱的执念，阻碍了他们去与员工沟通解决问题。

lines.text: As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect.
lines.translation: 结果，他们忽视了那些起初可能只是微不足道的小问题，直到不幸地，这些问题由于被搁置而不可避免地演变成重大问题或危机。

lines.text: As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer term strategic goals and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations, and to give regular feedback.
lines.translation: 作为领导者，人们期望他们能够激励团队追求长远战略目标；同时，从不那么宏大但更务实的角度来说，也期望他们能监督日常产出、设定清晰的预期并提供定期反馈。

lines.text: When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter.
lines.translation: 当在处理极具吸引力的收件箱和其他更重要的活动之间做出选择时，许多人牺牲了后者。

lines.text: Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress.
lines.translation: 日常的邮件需求对他们的工作目标进展产生了负面影响。

lines.text: This is because leaders must divert resources from other tasks to check, filter and respond to emails.
lines.translation: 这是因为领导者必须从其他任务中抽调资源来查看、筛选和回复邮件。

lines.text: The solution is cultivating self-control which is like a muscle-it can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise.
lines.translation: 解决办法是培养自控力，这就像肌肉一样——可以通过锻炼随着时间的推移不断增强和改善。

lines.text: Some suggestions include making space in your diary for the only periods during which you'll be checking emails, setting a timer for yourself so you don't become distracted by your inbox for too long, turning off email alerts so you're not interrupted by them.
lines.translation: 一些建议包括：在日程表上专门留出专门用来检查邮件的时间段；给自己设置一个定时器，免得在收件箱上分神太久；关闭邮件提醒，避免被它们打断思路。

lines.speaker: Q12.
lines.text: What does the speaker say is a common problem with managers?
lines.translation: 发言者说管理者的一个常见问题是什么？

lines.speaker: Q13.
lines.text: What may happen when managers ignore minor problems?
lines.translation: 当管理者忽视小问题时可能会发生什么？

lines.speaker: Q14.
lines.text: What are leaders expected to do in pursuing their strategic goals?
lines.translation: 人们期望领导者在追求其战略目标时做些什么？

lines.speaker: Q15.
lines.text: How can a manager best avoid being distracted by email?
lines.translation: 管理者怎样才能最好地避免被电子邮件分散注意力？

lines.text: In last week's lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems.
lines.translation: 在上周的讲座中，我们谈到了不良饮食习惯引起的问题，并重点讨论了医疗专业人员是如何试图解决这些问题的。

lines.text: Today, we'll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field-marketing.
lines.translation: 今天我们将继续这个话题，但重点关注一个不同领域的研——营销学。

lines.text: Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition?
lines.translation: 那么，关于改善营养，营销学能带给我们什么启示呢？

lines.text: Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food and how that influences food choices.
lines.translation: 一个由营销学教授组成的团队研究了食物视觉外观的重要性，以及它是如何影响人们的食物选择的。

lines.text: Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating.
lines.translation: 这些营销专家断言，食物外观带来的影响远比我们想象的要大，而且这可能是鼓励更健康饮食的关键钥匙。

lines.text: So how important is the appearance of food?
lines.translation: 那么食物的外观到底有多重要呢？

lines.text: Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger.
lines.translation: 研究表明，例如，仅仅在广告中看到一张诱人的汉堡照片，就能让人脑补出那个汉堡的味道或气味。

lines.text: This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it.
lines.translation: 这会让他们更有可能去购买并吃掉它。

lines.text: Of course, that's the point of advertisements.
lines.translation: 当然，这正是广告的目的所在。

lines.text: So isn't that a good thing?
lines.translation: 那这不是件好事吗？

lines.text: Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods, such as hamburgers and pizza, may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis.
lines.translation: 然而，营销学教授们认为这其实是个问题，因为诱人的美感加上唾手可得的不健康食品（如汉堡和披萨），可能会加剧全球性的健康危机。

lines.text: In fact, statistics show that 39% of all adults in the world weigh too much and another 13% are obese.
lines.translation: 事实上，统计数据表明，世界上39%的成年人体重超标，另有13%的人患有肥胖症。

lines.text: Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar and calorie content.
lines.translation: 正如我们上次讨论的那样，医疗专业人员试图通过专注于不同食物中的营养成分来对抗肥胖流行病，他们强调碳水化合物、脂肪、糖分和卡路里含量等指标。

lines.text: But they've had limited success.
lines.translation: 但他们收效甚微。

lines.text: The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food.
lines.translation: 营销学教授们认为，解决肥胖问题的真正方法是让食物看起来赏心悦目，并把重点放在观赏和食用这种食物带来的双重愉悦感上。

lines.text: That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices.
lines.translation: 这种愉悦感可以作为推广健康饮食选择的工具。

lines.text: In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it.
lines.translation: 事实上，该团队进行的研究表明，将健康食物与令人愉悦的画面、体验和情感联系在一起，能够让人产生更浓厚的购买或食用兴趣。

lines.text: "This is a better strategy," they claim, then reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them.
lines.translation: 他们声称：“这是一种更好的策略，”而不是一味生硬地提醒消费者某种食物对他们身体有好处。

lines.text: But are they right?
lines.translation: 但他们说得对吗？

lines.text: Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots.
lines.translation: 研究人员引用了一个旨在扭转胡萝卜销量下滑趋势的营销案例。

lines.text: The campaign didn't emphasize the carrots' healthy qualities, but embrace their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them.
lines.translation: 该营销活动并没有去强调胡萝卜的健康品质，而是大肆宣传它们的美感以及食用它们所获得的乐趣。

lines.text: For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots.
lines.translation: 例如，广告重点展示了胡萝卜鲜艳美丽的橙色和爽脆的质地。

lines.text: The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%.
lines.translation: 这场营销活动使产品销量实现了超过10%的惊人增长。

lines.text: The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.
lines.translation: 研究人员相信，其他公司也可以通过类似的广告来刺激健康食品的销售，将它们的产品描绘得极具吸引力且是快乐的源泉。

lines.speaker: Q16.
lines.text: What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied?
lines.translation: 发言者说一个营销学教授团队研究了什么？

lines.speaker: Q17.
lines.text: How have medical professionals tried to fight obesity?
lines.translation: 医疗专业人员是如何试图对抗肥胖症的？

lines.speaker: Q18.
lines.text: What can other companies learn from the example of the carrot promotion campaign?
lines.translation: 其他公司可以从胡萝卜促销活动这一案例中学到什么？

lines.text: The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s.
lines.translation: 家用清洁用品行业真正开始腾飞是在20世纪50年代。

lines.text: Prior to that resourceful housewives, who had grown up in a less prosperous era, relied on substances that they used in their kitchens such as vinegar used to clean windows.
lines.translation: 在那之前，在物质不那么充裕的时代长大的、精打细算的家庭主妇们，通常依赖厨房里的已有物质，比如用醋来擦窗户。

lines.text: Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year and is dominated by large global companies.
lines.translation: 如今，家用清洁用品行业年产值达数十亿美元，并被大型跨国公司所垄断。

lines.text: In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they're doing good business, too.
lines.translation: 然而，近年来，许多国家涌现出大量提供更环保清洁产品的小型企业和公司，而且他们的生意也做得红红火火。

lines.text: One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues.
lines.translation: 原因之一是消费者的环保和可持续发展意识正在不断增强。

lines.text: They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals.
lines.translation: 他们也希望把家变成一个安全的避风港，远离有毒化学物质。

lines.text: The third reason is people's awareness of a knowledge about technology has never been greater.
lines.translation: 第三个原因是人们对科技的认识和了解达到了前所未有的高度。

lines.text: In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology's ability to do what was once thought impossible.
lines.translation: 在过去，人们可能会对一种声称能达到惊人清洁效果的新产品持怀疑态度，但他们现在坚信科技有能力实现曾经被认为不可能的事情。

lines.text: There is perhaps no better example of this than a patented cloth sold by one company, which remarkably uses only water rather than traditional cleaning products.
lines.translation: 最典型的例子莫过于某家公司销售的一种专利抹布，它神奇地只需要水，而完全不需要传统清洁剂。

lines.text: The company claims its cloth lifts, traps and removes dirt and bacteria.
lines.translation: 该公司声称其抹布能够吸附、锁住并清除污垢和细菌。

lines.text: And considering that people don't see these products in shops, or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.
lines.translation: 考虑到人们在商店里看不到这些产品，在电视或平面媒体上也看不到它们的广告，这算得上是一次相当迅猛的崛起。

lines.text: Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets.
lines.translation: 这些公司背后的许多创始人在一开始都是通过在当地集市上摆摊销售，来测试其产品的可行性。

lines.text: Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues.
lines.translation: 然后，在许多情况下，是顾客们自发在社交媒体上留言跟帖，赞美它们的好处，从而帮这些产品做了营销。

lines.text: There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness and the benefits of having a clean home.
lines.translation: 还有专门致力于倡导保持房屋整洁干净以及干净的家所带来种种好处的电视节目和书籍。

lines.text: Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people feel they can control in an increasingly out-of-control world.
lines.translation: 在这个日益让人感到失控的世界里，拥有一个安全、干净的家，或许是人们觉得自己能掌控的为数不多的事情之一。

lines.text: And there are social media celebrities.
lines.translation: 此外还有社交媒体网红的助力。

lines.text: One woman in Britain has become a social media sensation with more than two million followers for her cleaning tips page.
lines.translation: 英国有一位女士因其清洁小妙招页面而轰动社交网络，吸引了200多万粉丝关注。

lines.speaker: Q19.
lines.text: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?
lines.translation: 发言者关于近年来的清洁用品行业说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q20.
lines.text: Why are newly developed cleaning products selling well?
lines.translation: 为什么新开发的清洁产品卖得很好？

lines.speaker: Q21.
lines.text: What are some customers doing to help promote non-traditional cleaning products?
lines.translation: 一些顾客正在做些什么来帮助推广非传统清洁产品？

lines.text: Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual, throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true.
lines.translation: 把零钱扔进喷泉是一个历史悠久的仪式：朝水里扔一枚便士，你的愿望就可能会实现。

lines.text: But all that money has to go somewhere.
lines.translation: 但所有这些钱总得有个去处。

lines.text: Otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters and euros could clog up the fountain's works.
lines.translation: 否则，越堆越多的便士、25美分和欧元硬币可能会堵塞喷泉的运转机构。

lines.text: Today, I'm going to talk about where all the coins go.
lines.translation: 今天，我就来谈谈这些硬币都去了哪里。

lines.text: Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places-from fountain maintenance to charity or public service.
lines.translation: 这些收集上来的硬币会流向各种不同的地方——从维护喷泉本身到慈善机构或公共服务。

lines.text: In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountains' maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don't mind getting their hands wet often get to it first.
lines.translation: 例如在纽约市，从公立公园喷泉里收集到的硬币通常用于喷泉自身的日常维护，不过一些不介意把手弄湿的民间“淘金创客”往往会捷足先登。

lines.text: There are over 50 beautiful, decorative display fountains in New York City parks.
lines.translation: 纽约市公园里有50多个美丽、兼具装饰性的观赏喷泉。

lines.text: They are cleaned by the parks' staff every few weeks.
lines.translation: 公园的工作人员每隔几周就会对它们进行一次大清洗。

lines.text: But most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
lines.translation: 但大部分硬币早已经被那些有门路的纽约人捞走了，剩下的可收集数量微乎其微。

lines.text: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul.
lines.translation: 不过，其他城市可能会捞到大得多的数目。

lines.text: Take for example, Rome's famous Trevi fountain, for hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return.
lines.translation: 以罗马著名的特雷维喷泉（许愿池）为例。数百年来，游客们都会背对池子，把硬币从肩膀上方扔进池中，以祈求重返罗马。

lines.text: So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day.
lines.translation: 扔钱的游客实在太多了，以至于罗马官员每天晚上都要清理喷泉，据报道，每天能清理出多达4000美元来自世界各地的零钱。

lines.text: Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy.
lines.translation: 每晚收集的大部分资金都用于资助一家为穷人服务的爱心超市。

lines.text: And collecting that cash is serious business.
lines.translation: 而且，收缴这笔现金绝非儿戏，是一项极为严肃的工作。

lines.text: Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain.
lines.translation: 众所周知，罗马官方对任何被抓到从喷泉里偷捞硬币的人都惩罚严厉。

lines.text: In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them.
lines.translation: 在2005年的一个案例中，四名喷泉清洁工在清理硬币时，被发现偷偷把硬币塞进自己的口袋，随后被警方逮捕。

lines.text: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
lines.translation: 最终，有关部门抓获了一名叫托马斯·摩根的臭名昭著的小偷，并禁止他靠近喷泉。在长达34年的时间里，他利用磁力棒捞走了数千美元的零钱。

lines.text: For the most part, money collected from privately-owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity.
lines.translation: 在美国，绝大多数从私人拥有的喷泉中收集上来的钱也会捐给慈善机构。

lines.text: The fountain in New York City's Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not-for-profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain's own maintenance.
lines.translation: 纽约市布莱恩特公园的喷泉由一家非营利公司拥有并运营，该公司将清洁工收集到的现金用于喷泉自身的维护费用。

lines.text: Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains and ponds in Florida's Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state.
lines.translation: 每年，从佛罗里达州华特迪士尼世界的许愿井、喷泉和池塘里捞出来的数万美元硬币，都会被捐赠出去，用以资助该州的寄养儿童。

lines.text: Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.
lines.translation: 无论你往喷泉里扔了硬币后愿望能否实现，你都可以放心，因为这笔零钱很可能流向了真正需要它的人手中。

lines.speaker: Q22.
lines.text: What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains?
lines.translation: 喷泉里越堆越多的硬币可能会引发什么问题？

lines.speaker: Q23.
lines.text: What does the speaker say about the coins collected from New York City's park fountains?
lines.translation: 发言者关于从纽约市公园喷泉收集的硬币说了什么？

lines.speaker: Q24.
lines.text: What do we learn about the money collected from Rome's Trevi Fountain?
lines.translation: 我们了解到关于从罗马特雷维喷泉（许愿池）收集来的钱的什么信息？

lines.speaker: Q25.
lines.text: What does the speaker say about Thomas Morgan?
lines.translation: 发言者关于托马斯·摩根说了什么？
